why_it_works: In 2025 banks and government signed a 'landmark' Rs1.225 trillion deal to resolve circular debt — and the very next fiscal year it grew by another Rs364 billion anyway, because the deal restructured the existing debt stock without touching the two things that generate new debt every year: DISCO losses and take-or-pay capacity payments to IPPs.

why_it_works: The 7th NFC Award's formula was written in 2010 — eight years before the FATA-KP merger — and has simply been extended ever since without being rewritten to account for the merged districts' population, so KP is now suing the federal government in the Federal Constitutional Court over ~Rs964bn it says never reached them under a formula built for a map of Pakistan that no longer exists.

why_it_works: Balochistan has produced more of Pakistan's gas than any other province since the 1950s and has the lowest access to it of any province today — a nearly 70-year-old contradiction that sits underneath a resource-rich-but-poorest-province paradox (Sui gas, Reko Diq, Gwadar) and a security cycle that independent analysts, not just advocacy groups, describe as self-reinforcing rather than resolving.

why_it_works: In September 2025 Pakistan signed a Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia treating an attack on either as an attack on both, expanded into a trilateral Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Turkey in August 2026 — Pakistan has since deployed troops, fighter aircraft, drones and an air-defense system to Saudi Arabia, and all three countries are discussing joint production of Turkey's KAAN fighter jet, so the real question is what a cash-strapped Pakistan is committing militarily in exchange for roughly $5.8B in Saudi investment and loans.

topic: Why Pakistan's tax code makes it cheaper to buy cotton from Brazil than from a Pakistani farmer
why_it_works: Pakistan's textile sector is its single largest dollar earner, yet cotton production has collapsed from a 2011-12 peak of 14.8 million bales to around 5.5 million bales today, and exports grew just 0.26% in FY26 — driven partly by an Export Facilitation Scheme that exempts imported cotton, yarn, and fabric from 18% GST while taxing the same locally-produced inputs at 18%, so the policy meant to support exporters is quietly accelerating the collapse of the domestic cotton farming it depends on.

why_it_works: Passed in April 2010, the 18th Amendment devolved administrative and financial power to Pakistan's provinces, abolished the concurrent legislative list, and reversed Musharraf-era centralization — it's the direct constitutional origin of the NFC Award formula and the provincial resource-control fights (Balochistan's gas royalties among them) already covered on this channel, making it the prequel most viewers have never actually seen explained.

topic: The 1972 policy that explains why Pakistan has so many money-losing state companies to begin with
why_it_works: In January 1972, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's government nationalized 31 major industrial units overnight — metals, heavy engineering, electricals, petrochemicals, cement, utilities, later extended to cotton ginning, rice husking, and flour mills in 1976 — meant to break the wealth concentration of the Ayub era, but instead followed by a 795% jump in the current account deficit and, per a 1980s government-appointed commission, chronic mismanagement across the nationalized sector; this is the direct historical ancestor of PIA, Pakistan Steel Mills, and Utility Stores Corporation, all already covered on this channel.
